title: Ability-Residual Decoupled Modeling for Affective Cognitive Diagnosis
abstract: arXiv:2609.21214v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Cognitive diagnosis infers students' concept mastery from response logs. However, students' responses are not determined by mastery alone: non-cognitive factors such as emotion, engagement, and fatigue can also affect performance. Affective cognitive diagnosis therefore extends conventional cognitive diagnosis by incorporating affective states. Existing methods often assume that the cognitive diagnosis backbone has already explained ability, item, and concept effects, so the remaining errors can be attributed mainly to affect. We argue that this assumption can be insufficient in real educational data: item calibration bias, systematic concept bias, personalized student-concept deviations, and latent student-item matching can form stable cognitive residuals. translated_title: 面向情感认知诊断的能力-残差解耦建模
translated_abstract: 认知诊断从学生的作答记录中推断其概念掌握程度。然而，学生的作答并非仅由掌握程度决定：情绪、投入度和疲劳等非认知因素也会影响表现。因此，情感认知诊断通过引入情感状态对传统认知诊断进行了扩展。现有方法通常假设认知诊断主干模型已经解释了能力、题目和概念的影响，因而剩余误差可以主要归因于情感因素。我们认为这一假设在真实教育数据中可能并不充分：题目标定偏差、系统性概念偏差、个性化的学生-概念偏差以及潜在的学生-题目匹配都可能形成稳定的认知残差。在缺乏显式建模路径的情况下，这些残差可能会泄漏到情感表示中，产生情感污染。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种能力-残差……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文针对现有情感认知诊断方法中认知残差泄漏到情感表示造成情感污染的问题，提出能力-残差解耦建模方法，显式建模题目偏差、概念偏差等稳定认知残差，从而提升情感认知诊断的准确性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an ability-residual decoupled modeling approach for affective cognitive diagnosis, which explicitly models stable cognitive residuals (e.g., item calibration bias and concept bias) to prevent them from leaking into affective representations and causing affect contamination.
